title: Fire Emblem Turned Off Permadeath in a Game That Never Left Japan
hook:
Fire Emblem's Casual Mode debuted on July 15, 2010 in a DS game Nintendo never sold outside Japan, and the Awakening team argued about it right up to launch. Do you play Classic or Casual?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Fire Emblem let you switch off permanent death for the first time in twenty ten, in a game that never left Japan? For twenty years, losing a unit in Fire Emblem meant losing them for good. That changed with New Mystery of the Emblem, a DS remake released in Japan on July fifteenth, twenty ten. It added two settings at the start of the game. Classic kept permanent death. Casual brought fallen characters back for the next chapter. In Nintendo's Iwata Asks interview, director Kouhei Maeda said permanent death gave the series its identity. The team worried that beginners would be scared off, and spent months deciding before adding the option. Nintendo never sold that game outside Japan, so most Western players had no idea it existed. They finally got Casual Mode with Fire Emblem Awakening on the 3DS in February twenty thirteen. Even then the developers were split. Project manager Masahiro Higuchi admitted he argued against Casual Mode right up to the end. The gamble paid off. Nintendo said Awakening sold one hundred eighty thousand copies in its first month in America, the best start in the history of the series. A mode built for beginners helped save the whole franchise. Do you play Fire Emblem on Classic or Casual? Follow for more gaming history.
